173. **A fill-in blank drawn as a line, and a run of no-break spaces in a formula's text one space.** Rob checked Round 40's *Introductory Business Statistics 2e* PDF with PDF4WCAG, whose machine checks are veraPDF's WCAG 2.2 profile (2026-11-04, 19:07): "Page 920: "Space characters are used for formatting purpose" under the radical sign in Table B2"; "Page 6 and many more: "ASCII text is used as a pseudographics". These are the blanks for answers to exercises. I thought we had handled these already?"; and "quite a few missing alt flags, but mostly for links in reference lists where we know this is not a real violation", which are 2.4.9-1's, a reference list's bare addresses (`docs/bare-links.md`). **Why the blanks still failed**: the ActualText "blank" each blank's Span got (Round 7 of the LibreTexts book, item 33's code) is what a screen reader says, and the rule doesn't read it. Rule 1.3.1-1 (`SARepeatedCharacters`, `isNonSpace == false || numberOfRepeatedCharacters < 5`) is fed by wcag-algs' `SemanticDocumentPostprocessingConsumer.checkForRepeatedCharacters`, which takes the text chunks of each `SemanticSpan` in the structure's order, a figure's and code's passed over, chains those on one baseline whose touching characters match or are both white space, and counts each run, a digit's aside; a chunk's value is its glyphs' Unicode (read in veraPDF-wcag-algs and veraPDF-validation at v1.30.3, cloned for reading, 2026-11-04). The docs said as much ("still fails one of five or more", checking.md, formats.md, the CHANGELOG): the earlier round knew the check would still fail and left it so. A scan of the old PDF's text following the rule (`scan131b.py`, below) finds 453 blanks of five or more underscores, the first on PDF page 22, printed page 6 ("6. Data _____"; "1. Population ____" above it has four), and the radical's six spaces on PDF page 936, printed 920. **The blanks now**: in a tagged PDF, `PDF_MACROS` draws each blank as a line as the page is shipped out, a rule where its underscores' ink was, from the first's to the last's, at the underscore's height and as thick, with kerns either side keeping the line of text as wide; the rule takes the first underscore's attributes, so it's in the Span's marked content, which tagpdf, run after it, opens around it (LATEX-NOTES, Artifacts and LuaTeX). The underscores go, so the text has nothing of the blank, and its Span still says "blank". veraPDF reads such a Span as line art and types it a figure (`AccumulatedNodeConsumer.acceptSemanticImage`), so its 4.1.2-17 ("Redundant span", `correctType != null`) passes. The measure is the face's: luaotfload's `descriptions` for a face it shapes, and HarfBuzz's glyph extents for one HarfBuzz shapes (`Renderer=HarfBuzz`), which has no `descriptions`, each scaled across by the underscore's width and up by its depth, so a face stretched wider (`FakeStretch`) has a line as long as its underscores and no thicker (LATEX-NOTES, Fonts). A run of underscores ends where its face or its marked content does, so a blank and an italic one beside it, or one in a span beside it, are two lines, each in its own Span. A first version kept the blank's first underscore as text, for a copy from a viewer that doesn't take ActualText, and drew the rest; renderers draw a rule that thin as whole pixels and a glyph shaded, so at 96 and 150 pixels an inch the kept underscore looked like a dash of its own beside the line (poppler and Ghostscript), and it went: copying from such a viewer gives nothing for a blank now. Kept as underscores: a blank in a face with no measure, as one loaded from TeX's own metrics (`ec-lmr10`), which the log names after the last page, with how many (`TextbookImprover blanks kept: N, in the face`, the face's PostScript name or TeX's on the line after, which fits a line of TeX's log), and `build-pdf.py` and a deck's PDF warn of (written first from LuaTeX's `stop_run` callback, which took the place of LuaTeX's own last lines, "Output written on" with the PDF's pages among them, so a deck's count of pages read 0, as the slides suite found; LATEX-NOTES, LuaTeX); a blank in an untagged PDF, which has no ActualText to give its text (a blank is drawn only where tagpdf is loaded and the blank's glyph has its marked-content attribute); and a LuaTeX without `pre_shipout_filter`, and a build with `OER_BLANK_GLYPHS`, which only the suites set. **Blanks of three and of two**: the first rebuild's text still had three runs of six underscores in contingency tables' rows, which veraPDF chains across cells on one baseline, where a run of four or more had been a blank: two on PDF page 235, cells of three side by side ("Men______1455", "Total___41______"), and one on page 239, three cells of two ("Total______1"). A run of three is a blank now, never drawn shorter, three being the least one is drawn at, and the second rebuild had page 239's alone; a run of two is a blank now where it stands apart, as those cells' and "( __ , __ )" have it, and not where it's joined to a letter or a digit (Python's `__init__`), a character outside ASCII, whose letters Lua's patterns can't tell from its punctuation (`café__`, `“__”` too), or anything that isn't text, emphasis or a formula (`*word*__`). The suite's reader of a page's text leaves an artifact's out, as veraPDF does: a cell of a row of four begins with an artifact's space, which had made three spaces of two. **Two blanks with a space between them**: drawn as lines, they'd leave the space before, between, and after them side by side in the text, three, which 1.3.1-2 reports. *Microbiology* asks for answers of two words so six times ("The ________ ________ prevents access of microbes in the blood"), three of them between words. `pdf-target.lua` makes blanks with nothing but spaces between them one Span, `\OERBlanks{2}{…}`, its ActualText "blank blank", and `PDF_MACROS` gives the spaces between two it draws no character (tagpdf's `g__tag_interwordspaceOff_attr`, set before tagpdf writes its spaces), so a screen reader still hears two blanks. The spaces are a space or a line's end in the source and any of Unicode's in the text: a no-break space as the writer writes it (`~`), a narrow one too (`\,`), and the rest as phantoms of themselves (PANDOC-NOTES, The LaTeX writer, for a tagged PDF); and a blank in bold or italics alone (`**________**`, `\textbf{…}` in the group) is one of the blanks. The grouping reads a paragraph's whole list of inlines, where it had read a `Str` at a time. **Table B2's radical**: the source sets the square root's sign over an `mtable` of two rows of no-break spaces, which texmath writes `\text{~~}` and `\text{~~~~~~}` (PANDOC-NOTES, the HTML reader), and tagpdf writes a space character for each tilde. `pdf-target.lua`'s `Math` keeps the first of a run of two or more tildes in `\text`, in the `\textbf`, `\textit`, and `\texttt` texmath writes for a bold, italic, or monospace `mtext`, and in `\mbox`, `\textrm`, `\textup`, `\textnormal`, `\textmd`, `\textsf`, and `\textsl`, and makes the rest an `\hphantom`, which keeps the width; a formula of nothing but such text keeps none, the paragraph's spaces either side of it being two already. The formula's MathML `mtext` has the one no-break space, or none (LATEX-NOTES, Math). The counts of a table's columns take an `\hphantom` as what's in its braces (`DRAWS_NOTHING`), where it had added one character. A heading's bookmark, which shows a formula as its LaTeX (the writer's `\texorpdfstring`, the formula's text as Pandoc stringifies it), shows the `\hphantom` too; left. A formula in raw LaTeX in a Markdown page isn't a formula to Pandoc, and is left. OpenStax's books have 1,928 `mtext`s of nothing but white space with two or more no-break spaces, and 264 with words beside a run of them, each one space in the text now. **The book**: rebuilt four times as the code grew, the last with the review's fixes (cd8f43d, on 42f89d0; the mailbox's code differs from it only in where it writes its report of kept blanks, of which the book has none, and `main`'s new commits change only decks), 953 pages, PDF 2.0. Its 540 blanks are each a Span "blank" holding a line and no character, none kept as underscores and no warning, and Table B2's radical has one space in each of its two rows; the scan finds no run of five underscores or of three spaces, where the old PDF had 453 and one. It reports two runs of its own making: ten commas on PDF page 53, set 3.8 points above the 19s between them, and five primes on page 539, superscripts of separate formulas 4.7 points above the line, which it puts on a line of their own since it groups glyphs by height alone, where veraPDF's chain goes from chunk to chunk in the structure's order and ends at a character of another height (by its source). veraPDF's PDF/UA-2 profile finds nothing (the output check), whose other six findings are its advice on a header cell holding only a formula. Sent to Rob for PDF4WCAG. **Not verified**: veraPDF's WCAG modules can't run here (Maven Central refused the download with 403, and building them from their source wasn't allowed), so the findings themselves are for PDF4WCAG or `check-output.py --wcag` where the modules are installed; the scan is a stand-in that follows the rule's source, run on the PDF's text outside artifacts, per line and in the order shown, where veraPDF chains in the structure's order. Not tried: a screen reader on a Span that holds only a line. **Checks**: the PDF suite's book of blanks, built twice, as lines and as underscores (`OER_BLANK_GLYPHS`): each blank's line where its underscores' ink was, each end, its foot, and its top within 0.02 points, in IBM Plex Serif upright, italic (whose underscore stands left of its advance), and bold, in a list, at a paragraph's end, drawn shorter, in a table's cell, in a note, of three, of three and of two side by side in a table's cells, and joined to a number, each in its Span's marked content, which holds no character; two blanks with a space, a no-break space, or a thin space and a space between them one Span, "blank blank", a bold one among them too; a blank and an italic one beside it, and a blank and one in a span beside it, two lines in two Spans; the text with no run of five of a character but a space, nor of three spaces, but a heading's underscores, which aren't a blank; `__init__` and `café__` kept; every other character where the underscores' build has it; the formulas' runs, plain and bold, one space and a phantom, and a formula of spaces alone none; and veraPDF finding nothing. Three more books, built as a build draws them: blanks in a face HarfBuzz shapes, drawn in its underscore's measure, in one Span, no space between them; one in that face stretched half as wide again, a line as thick as the underscore and half again as long; two in a face loaded from TeX's metrics, kept with their space, and the build's warning naming `ec-lmr10`; and an untagged PDF's, kept, nothing drawn, nothing said. The book, the notes book, and the fit book are built with `OER_BLANK_GLYPHS`, since their checks count underscores where they're drawn. With the mailbox applied by `git am -3` to a fresh clone of GitHub's `main` at e174427, every suite passes in `313` (2,017 s) and the PDF suite with TinyTeX (`tiny`, 1,369 s), skipping what `main` skips here, veraPDF's WCAG modules among it. The first full run found the report of kept blanks taking LuaTeX's last lines (above) and the unit suite's count of the macros' chunks of Lua, which counts the report's now.

174. **Round 44's review, and what it found.** A reviewer given the round's work as commits (4c39f67), a brief of what it was for, and the PDF suite's tools, not my account of having tested it, found nine defects, each reproduced in a book of its own, and gaps in the checks; each is put right, and the checks above catch each now. **An untagged PDF lost its blanks' text**: with no structure tree there's no ActualText, and the underscores were taken out all the same ("knownas / The preventsaccess"); a blank is drawn now only where its glyph has tagpdf's marked-content attribute (LATEX-NOTES, Artifacts). **A face without luaotfload's measure lost the space between grouped blanks**, the attribute that takes back tagpdf's space set at every space in a group whether its blanks were drawn or not ("The ________________ prevents"), and nothing said the blanks weren't drawn: HarfBuzz-mode faces have no `descriptions`, as faces from TeX's metrics don't. The space is taken back now only between two blanks drawn, HarfBuzz's own measure is read, and a face with neither is named in a warning. **Grouping missed** a bold blank beside a plain one ("Bold   after", three spaces), a no-break space and a space between two blanks (four), and a thin space between them, which veraPDF counts as white space (U+2009; its `isWhiteSpaceChar` adds U+00A0, U+2007, and U+202F to Java's): the grouping reads a paragraph's inlines whole now (item 173). **`one_space` missed** the `\textbf`, `\textit`, and `\texttt` texmath writes for styled `mtext`, and a formula of spaces alone between two words kept a space, three in a row with the paragraph's. **The run of two's test was ASCII's and a `Str`'s**: `café__`, `μ__`, `日本__`, and `*word*__` became blanks. **Two blanks with nothing between them in two faces were one line**, in the first's face and Span, the second Span empty. **The table counts took `one_space`'s `\hphantom` for a character** (a column's share 0.2490 where it had been 0.2123, in the reviewer's table). **A heading's bookmark shows the `\hphantom`** (cosmetic; left, and said in the docs). **Two comments** still said a blank was four underscores or more. And by reading, the line's thickness was scaled by the face's width, too thick in a face stretched wider; it's scaled by the underscore's depth now (item 173). Found sound by the review: the callbacks' order (`linksplit`, `oer.blanks.rules`, then tagpdf's two); a line within 0.02 points of its ink and in its Span for a blank hung into the margin by protrusion, in nested boxes, in a group broken across lines, and on a page of two columns, every other character in place (269 of 269); a footnote's mark after a blank, a colored blank, a blank in `\fbox`; `one_space` keeping every glyph's place (334 of 334), and harmless in nested braces, inside `\sqrt` and a matrix, and done twice; a deck's PDF, its blanks drawn and veraPDF's ua2, wt1a, and wt1r profiles passing. Not tried by it either: veraPDF's WCAG modules, a screen reader, form XObjects (which `pre_shipout_filter` doesn't see), and a page shipped twice. **Mutations**: 32, each a part of the round's code taken out or changed, the drawn blanks' case built and checked with each (`mut44.py`, in `313`; the two of the report of kept blanks run again on its last form): 30 caught, every finding's fix among them, and two missed, each a guard that another test covers in every case the filter writes: a blank drawn where its own glyph has no marked content (the draw needs tagpdf's attribute to exist at all, and an untagged PDF's LaTeX, with no `\DocumentMetadata`, never loads tagpdf, so no build here reaches the glyph's own test), and a run going on into another face (each blank is a Span of its own, so its marked content ends where its face could, the filter never setting two faces in one blank). Both are kept, for LaTeX written by hand.

175. **A face with a STAT table that isn't a variable font embedded from its file.** Rob opened the PDF of *Introductory Business Statistics 2e* from Round 44 in Acrobat (2026-11-05, 13:22): "When opening the Intro Business Statistics PDF in Acrobat, I received the attached error about the embedded font", the dialog reading "Cannot extract the embedded font 'XKSRKX+NotoSans-Regular'. Some characters may not display or print correctly." It isn't new: Round 40's PDF has the same subset. **What's different about that face**: of the PDF's eight TrueType programs, NotoSans-Regular's two subsets (XKSRKX, DFOEUF) and NotoSans-Bold's (AITKSB) had no glyph with instructions and no composite glyph, where the italics' and Noto Sans Math's simple glyphs all have instructions and their composites are kept (fontTools, 2026-11-05). Noto Sans 2.008's regular and bold have a STAT table and its italics don't; the font loader counts a STAT table as variable data (`readers.stat`), and luaotfload 3.29's patch of `trytosharefont` gives any font with variable data a glyph stream provider, as for a variable font at its default (`luaotfload-features.lua`, the same on upstream's `main`); LuaTeX then writes each glyph from luaotfload's copy of the outlines, without instructions and with composites merged, and fills the slots it still adds for a composite's parts with whatever glyph the face has at each slot's number, at the part's width: XKSRKX's glyphs 5, 35, and 65, the parts of its ŷ and ī, drew the straight quote, the at sign, and the caret (LATEX-NOTES, Fonts, read in the source and measured). Only XKSRKX of the three has such slots, AITKSB's composites' parts being drawn in their own right, and only XKSRKX was named. Every subset passes a strict reading of its tables, so which of the three, the missing hinting, the merged composites, or the misfilled slots, Acrobat rejects isn't known, and Acrobat can't run here. **Now**: `STATIC_FONTS` (`lib/latexbuild.py`) takes the provider away from a font whose variable data has no axes, fvar's, and that isn't a named instance, so such a face is embedded from its file, as its italics were. It comes before anything loads a face: fontspec loads the regular face where `\setmainfont` sets it, and in a probe without babel the text was set in that font, which the setting in the header-includes didn't reach; a book's text is in babel's family, loaded when the text is set, which a setting there does reach (LATEX-NOTES, Fonts), but the template's copy puts it ahead of whatever loads a face first. A book's LaTeX is written with a copy of Pandoc's own template with it before `$fonts.latex()$` (`book_template`), as the EPUB build copies Pandoc's epub3 template, the line the same in 3.9 (its source), 3.12.1, and 3.13, and the run warns where the line isn't there; a deck's macros, which its template reads before its faces, start with it. **Measured**: a small book in Noto Sans built from `main` embeds its regular and bold with no composite and no glyph with instructions, the slots' widths not their glyphs'; with the fix, 6 composites and 29 of 35 glyphs with instructions in the regular, every slot holding its part. The book rebuilt with the fix alone: XKSRKX has 129 glyphs, 11 composites, and 118 with instructions, AITKSB 83 of 88, DFOEUF 12 of 12, each slot its part, its widths matching its outline; all 1,379,472 characters are where Round 44's PDF has them; veraPDF's PDF/UA-2 profile finds nothing, and the output check finds the six `pdf-table-header-is-formula` it found before. That PDF went to Rob for Acrobat at 14:43, ahead of the mailbox. **Tests**: the PDF suite's book of math fonts has a target in TeX Live's Josefin Sans, which has a STAT table and no fvar, unhinted but drawing its accented letters from parts, where TeX has it (`josefin`, on the installation page now; `tiny` hasn't it, and skips the check): its regular and bold each draw an accented letter from its parts, each part drawn (`pdftext.truetype_glyphs`, which reads `loca` and `glyf` itself, so the suite needs nothing new); the unit suite checks the template's copy and the setting's Lua. **Mutations** (`mut45.py`, the math fonts' case): no template and the provider kept for a static face are caught; the setting put after the template's font settings, or in the header-includes, as it first was, is missed, since babel's family, the one a book's text is in, is loaded only when the text is set, after both, so the placement is a guard against whatever else loads a face first, not something a book's text needs now. Not done: a LaTeX book's tagged copy keeps the book's own fonts as it loads them, without the setting.

176. **A formula's run of spaces one character as LaTeX sets it, not by rewriting the formula.** What Round 44 left open (item 173): a heading's bookmark showed the `\hphantom` `pdf-target.lua` wrote in a formula's run of no-break spaces, and a formula in raw LaTeX in a Markdown page, which Pandoc's reader doesn't take for a formula, kept its runs; Rob asked for the open items (2026-11-05). **How tagpdf makes the characters** (LATEX-NOTES, Artifacts, read in `tagpdf.lua` 1.0c): `markspaces` marks a glue after or before a glyph, or after a user's penalty, as `\nobreak`'s is, as each box or paragraph is made, and passes over a formula's own spaces but not those of its `\text`, a box of its own; at shipout it writes a space before each marked glue whose attribute for no character is unset. **Now**: `pdf-target.lua` leaves the formula as written, and `PDF_MACROS` sets that attribute on each space of a run after its first once the formula is set (`post_mlist_to_hlist_filter`), a run going on through penalties, kerns, rules, and unmarked spaces, and from one box to the next, and ending at a character; and, as each page is shipped out, before tagpdf, on every space of a formula of spaces alone that has a marked space beside it on its line, which made three side by side with the paragraph's two. The widths are untouched, since only attributes change. A heading's bookmark has the formula's LaTeX as Pandoc's writer gives it, `a\text{~~~to~~~}b`, as any formula's is (PANDOC-NOTES, the LaTeX writer), without the phantom; a formula's MathML structure has the one space, being the page's marked content, and its attached MathML file the spaces as written. **Tests**: the drawn blanks' book has each formula in a paragraph of its own and adds a raw formula around a word, a raw formula of spaces alone, a formula of spaces alone between two letters, a space in each of three boxes, and a formula in a heading, and checks each line's text ("Aroundword 𝑥 or 𝑦", "Spacesonly  between", "Joined word", "Rawaround 𝑎 and 𝑏") and the heading's bookmark. **Mutations** (`mut45.py`, the drawn blanks' case): seven, each caught: runs not collapsed, a run ending at a box, a run never ending, a formula of spaces keeping one, every formula taken for spaces alone, the filter writing phantoms again, and no space needed beside a formula of spaces, which the book missed until it had one between two letters ("Joined word"), added for it. **The book**: rebuilt with both changes (953 pages, 3,044 seconds beside the suites), its fonts as with the font fix alone; every character but a space is where that build has it (1,168,144), and so is every space but one: Table B2's radical (PDF page 936, printed 920) has one space for its two rows of no-break spaces, the run going on from one row to the next, where the filter's rewrite left one in each row. The scan that follows veraPDF's rule (`scan45.py`, as `scan131b.py` was) finds no run of spaces or of a character but the two of its own making Round 44 found, a formula's commas and primes set at another height; veraPDF's PDF/UA-2 profile finds nothing, and the output check the same six findings. No bookmark of the book holds LaTeX, before or now: the bookmark Round 44's review found was in a book of its own.

177. **What Acrobat couldn't extract: the space, as luaotfload's copy of a face gives it.** Rob (2026-11-05, 17:12): "The PDF now opens with no error in Acrobat," of *Introductory Business Statistics 2e* rebuilt with item 175's setting. Which of item 175's three differences Acrobat had rejected, the missing hinting, the merged composites, or the misfilled parts, mattered for a variable font, which luaotfload still embeds from its own copy, so Rob opened 44 files that evening, each changing one thing (17:31 to 18:48; their builders in `r46/diag`, `r46/excerpt`, `r46/full`, `r46/allglyphs`, and `r46/vf`): **Small files**: five one-page files in Noto Sans 2.008 embedded from luaotfload's copy, one for each difference alone, the font from its file, and TeX Live's Junicode VF, all opened (17:31); so did page ii of Round 44's book, its program the one Acrobat named, as built and in six variants (17:52). **The whole book**, its 451 pictures made a pixel, 8 MB: as built, XKSRKX from the fixed build, and XKSRKX's three misfilled parts emptied each showed the message at once, naming XKSRKX, AITKSB, and XKSRKX; all three provider-embedded programs from the fixed build, none (17:59). With two of the three from the fixed build: the bold as built, the message (AITKSB); the second regular as built (DFOEUF, unicode-math's operator names, "STDEV" and "lim"), none; XKSRKX as built, the message (18:07). XKSRKX with its simple glyphs hinted from the fixed build, or with its composites and their parts from it, the rest as built: the message both times (18:16). **Pages of glyphs**: every glyph of XKSRKX, and of AITKSB, at the book's four sizes, each named its font (18:20); in groups, only the bold without its three f ligatures did (18:24); by group and size, the 56 regular glyphs the passing files had drawn, at four sizes or 12 points alone, all 125 at 12 points, the bold's first half, and all 85 bold at 12 or at 20.66 points did, and the other 69 regular glyphs and the bold's second half didn't (18:29). **The space**: every failing group held the space glyph, and no passing one did. luaotfload's `repackpoints` writes a glyph with no contours as a 10-byte header of zeros, which LuaTeX embeds padded to 12, where a font gives an empty glyph no record, its two `loca` entries equal, and LaTeX's tagging draws a real space between words; none of the small files was tagged. The 56 regular glyphs at 12 points and the bold's first half with those records emptied, and the whole book with every Noto Sans program as built but for them, opened; a page of nothing but the space, as built, didn't (18:33). Not every draw trips it: page ii's four spaces, in a 9.96-point footer, didn't, nor the em space's identical record drawn at four sizes. So it was the space's record, in a face embedded from luaotfload's copy, and none of the three: the hinting, the composites, and the parts made no difference alone. **Now**: `STATIC_FONTS` also wraps luaotfload's glyph stream provider where it's registered, under its own name, `luaotfload.harf.glyphstream` (an exclusive callback, which luaotfload's HarfBuzz mode has taken over for both modes before a document's first line), and gives a TrueType glyph's stream (mode 2) of no more than 12 bytes whose count of contours is 0 as empty, which LuaTeX writes as a font does; so a variable font, still embedded from luaotfload's copy, without its hinting, has its empty glyphs empty. TeX Live's Junicode VF in a tagged page at the book's four sizes has its space, glyph 3610, as 12 bytes of zeros without it and empty with it, the pages identical and veraPDF's PDF/UA-2 profile passing both; Acrobat showed the message for the first and not the second (Rob, 18:48). A face with a STAT table that isn't a variable font is still embedded from its file (item 175), its hinting, composites, and parts its own. **Tests**: the PDF suite's math fonts' book has a target in Junicode VF where TeX has it (`junicodevf`, on the installation page now), its program checked for any glyph with a record of no contours (`pdftext.empty_outlines`); the mutation that leaves the wrapper out is caught. **The reports**: `luaotfload-reports.md` replaces `luaotfload-stat-report.md`, two issues ready to file, the empty glyph's record first, since every variable TrueType font has it in node mode, then the STAT test, with mode 2's misfilled parts.

178. **A LaTeX book's tagged copy reads the font setting too.** What Round 45 left open (item 175): `STATIC_FONTS` reached a book's PDF from its pages, through Pandoc's template, and a deck's, but not a LaTeX book's tagged copy, which `pdf.from: book` builds and a `source` target with `tagging: "on"` writes, so a book that sets such a face itself, with fontspec or TeX Live's `josefin` package, embedded it as luaotfload embeds a variable font; Rob asked for the open items (2026-11-05, 17:12). **Now**: `tag` (`lib/texremediate.py`) writes the setting first after `\DocumentMetadata`, the one it adds or the book's own, before the class and everything else, under a comment saying what it's for, and not again in a copy made from a copy (`texremediate.STATIC_FONTS`). luaotfload's constructors are there by then, so the patch reaches every face the document loads (measured: Josefin Sans's regular and bold, set with fontspec, drew their accented letters from parts with it there and none without; LATEX-NOTES, Fonts). Every tagged copy has it, since whether a face has the table isn't known until LuaLaTeX loads it, and any other face is embedded as before; pdfLaTeX skips it, inside `\ifdefined\directlua`. The run doesn't mention it, as a book's PDF from its pages doesn't. **Tests**: the LaTeX suite's case of a book that sets Josefin Sans with fontspec, its tagged copy built with LuaLaTeX, each face drawing an accented letter from its parts, each part drawn, where TeX has Josefin Sans (`josefin`), skipped where it hasn't; the unit suite's check that the copy has it just after the `\DocumentMetadata` it adds, just after the book's own, and once in a copy made from a copy; and the source target's check of a tagged copy's first lines, which expected the class straight after `\DocumentMetadata` and failed once the setting was there, as the full LaTeX suite found, the spot runs having left that case out, expects the setting between them now. **Mutations** (`mut46.py`): no setting, the setting before `\begin{document}`, where fontspec has loaded the face already, and the setting written again in a copy of a copy, each caught.

179. **A heading's formula is its text in the heading's bookmark.** What Round 45 left open (item 176): a heading's bookmark had a formula's TeX, `Spaced a\text{~~~to~~~}b heading`, as Pandoc's writer makes a bookmark from the heading's text by `stringify`, in which a formula is its TeX (PANDOC-NOTES, the LaTeX writer); Rob asked for the open items (2026-11-05, 17:12). **Now**: the PDF filter's pass `bookmarks` (`pdf-target.lua`), after the formulas are fitted, sets each inline formula in a heading that Pandoc's plain writer writes as text in a `\texorpdfstring` of its own, `\texorpdfstring{\(...\)}{` raw, the text a Str, and `}` raw: `stringify` takes the Str and skips the raw LaTeX, so the writer's own `\texorpdfstring` around the heading has the text for the bookmark, and the heading, the contents, and the running head set the formula as before. The text is the plain writer's, in Unicode where texmath can, its spaces made a word's, a run of them one, and a script it puts in parentheses for want of a character, `ℝ^(n)`, written `ℝ^n`, as `deck-pptx.lua` writes a formula in a deck's notes; a formula whose last line is a comment gets the line end the writer would give it (`handleMathComment`), which Pandoc 3.9's Markdown reader can leave a formula with (PANDOC-NOTES, the Markdown reader). A formula the plain writer can't write, a fraction, a root, a matrix, a sum with limits, or a command texmath doesn't know, which it gives as `$TeX$` with a warning that it's rendered as TeX, is left as it was, its TeX in the bookmark; the filter records it (`OER_PDF_RECORD`), and `build-pdf.py` takes that warning out of what Pandoc said, with texmath's reason on the lines after it where it gives one, and a formula's second line as Pandoc indents it (PANDOC-NOTES, the plain writer on a formula), and says once how many headings' formulas are their TeX in the bookmarks, for a PDF, for a latex target's LaTeX, and for `--latex-only`. A display formula in a heading is the writer's. LaTeX's tagging titles a heading's structure element from the same argument with `\pdf_purify:nN`, which takes the caret the writer escapes, `\^{}`, for a combining circumflex: `ℝ^n` in the bookmark is `ℝ̂n` in the element's `/T` (LATEX-NOTES, Links, bookmarks, and text made plain). **Measured**: a small book's bookmarks read "Power x² + y₁ ≤ α and ℝ^n", "Spaced a to b heading", and "Fraction \frac{a}{b} and x̄_n", the run saying once of its PDF and once of its latex target's LaTeX that one formula is its TeX, with no warning of Pandoc's; Pandoc 3.12.1 writes the LaTeX 3.13 does. **Tests**: the unit suite runs the filter on headings, checking the LaTeX for each kind of formula, a display formula and one outside a heading among them, a command texmath doesn't know and a formula over two lines too, and the record, and gives what Pandoc said to the build's reading of it, which leaves none of its warnings; it checks the reading on warnings written out as well, a reason's lines, a formula's second line, and a third warning of a formula recorded twice, which stays, and its note; the PDF suite's drawn blanks' book checks its heading's bookmark, "Spaced a to b heading", and the LaTeX; the math fonts' book has a heading with x² + α, x̄ₙ, and a fraction, its bookmark "Scripted x² + α, x̄_n, and \frac{a}{b} heading", the note once for each of its PDFs, for its latex target, and for `--latex-only`, and no warning of Pandoc's. **Mutations** (`mut46.py`, 14 for the round, the 3 of item 178 among them): no pass, spaces not collapsed, the TeX taken for text, no line end after a comment, scripts kept in parentheses, texmath's spaces kept, the plain writer's warning kept, and no note for a PDF or for a latex target, each caught; no note for `--latex-only` and a display formula made inline were missed until the math fonts' book built the LaTeX alone and the unit check had a display formula in a heading, then caught. Reviewing the series before sending it found two shapes of the warning that the build's match, the warning's one line exactly, missed: a command texmath doesn't know, whose warning ends with a colon and texmath's reason on lines after it, and a formula over two lines, whose second line Pandoc indents; each was left on the terminal beside the note, and the build takes them out now. 182. **A heading's fraction, root, and limit are text in its bookmark.** What Round 46 left open (item 179): a formula the plain writer can't write kept its TeX in the bookmark, which "would want a writer texmath hasn't". **Measured first**: of the 554 formulas in titles in OpenStax's public repositories (242 different), the plain writer gave 89 as `$TeX$` with its warning, 50 holding a fraction, 31 a root, 14 a limit set as `\underset{x\rightarrow a}{\text{lim}}`, 3 an array, and 1 an arrow over a letter, `\overset{\rightarrow}{L}` (Pandoc 3.12.1, 2026-11-05; PANDOC-NOTES, the LaTeX writer). **Now**: `bin/math-text.lua`, which `pdf-target.lua` and `deck-pdf.lua` load with `dofile` from their own folder, writes those first, each in the formula's place as a character of Unicode's private use, U+E001 on, which texmath passes as an identifier, the plain writer writing the rest: `\frac`, `\dfrac`, `\tfrac`, and `\cfrac` as a/b, a part in parentheses where it's more than one term, (√x − 2)/(x − 4), a root one term; `\sqrt` as √x, ∛x, ∜x, or its index's superscripts before √, ⁿ√a, ¹⁰√x, the radicand in parentheses where it's more than one term, √(x + 1); `\underset` as the name, its subscript in parentheses, and a space after it where the name is a word, lim_(x → 4), lím too; `\overset` with an arrow as U+20D7 after the letter, L⃗, and with anything else as a superscript, =ᵃ; and `\overline` as U+0305 after each character, A̅B̅. A fraction or a root a script follows is in parentheses, (a/b)², (√x)², and so is a fraction where what's beside it would run into it, (1/2)x, a(b/c), (a/b)(c/d), ∫(P(x)/Q(x))dx, a mixed number set apart from its whole number instead, 2 1/3, and a root a letter, a digit, or a parenthesis follows, (√2)x; a limit's space after its name is a space beside the fraction after it, lim_(x → 4) (√x − 2)/(x − 4). A part that can't be written, a binomial in a fraction, leaves the whole formula its TeX. Then the text is made plain to read: its spaces a word's, a run of them one, the text trimmed; a script in parentheses in Unicode's superscripts or subscripts where each of its characters has one (the digits, signs, and parentheses, the Latin letters Unicode has, a few Greek ones, and a degree for `\circ`), its spaces dropped, ℝⁿ, x̄ₙ, xⁿ⁺¹, nᵗʰ, xₘₐₓ, 30°; otherwise with its mark, without its parentheses where it's ASCII's letters or digits that no letter or digit follows, x^q, and with them otherwise, 4^(π), ∫_(C)P dx; the innermost first and then the one it's in, up to three times, so that a degree in a superscript, ^(^(∘)), as texmath writes *Chemistry 2e*'s `H_{\text{f}}^{{^\circ}}`, is °. A script that holds one already keeps its parentheses, x^(2³), as the plain writer writes it. What's left as TeX is what the plain writer still warns of, a matrix, a binomial, or a command texmath doesn't know; the filter records the formula's TeX and the TeX of each part warned of (`bookmark_warned`), and the build takes those warnings out of what Pandoc said and says how many are TeX, as before. Of the 554, 551 are text now, and 3 keep their TeX, each an array. **Found on the way, changed before the commit**: a pass for a mark followed by one character, which texmath's output never has, made the first letter of a script the group pass had left a superscript, `x^{aq}` as xᵃq; each script's character mapped to itself, so that x^(2³) was x²³; `\vec` was among the arrows, a command texmath writes itself, v⃗; and a fraction ran into what was beside it, `2\frac{1}{3}` as 21/3 and `\frac{1}{2}x` as 1/2x, which a look at the corpus's fractions beside a letter found, *Calculus*' `\int{\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}dx,}` among them. A deck's PowerPoint notes keep the plain writer's text (`deck-pptx.lua`), which `math.from_text` reads back as the formula. **Tests**: the unit suite runs the module on 74 formulas with Pandoc's Lua, each kind above and the four it can't write; the filter on headings with a fraction and a root, a binomial, a command texmath doesn't know, a binomial over two lines, and a fraction of a binomial, its record and the warnings taken out; and the build's reading of a record whose warned parts aren't its formulas; the PDF suite's math fonts' book has a heading with x² + α, x̄ₙ, 4^(π), a/b, and a binomial, its bookmark "Scripted x² + α, x̄ₙ, 4^(π), a/b, and \binom{n}{k} heading"; and the decks suite's odd deck a slide with ℝⁿ, a/b, and a binomial; with Pandoc 3.12.1, 3.13, and the stand-in for 3.9, which runs 3.12.1's texmath. **Mutations**: 34 of the module, the filter's record, and the build's reading (`mathtext.log`), each caught, an escaped brace once the unit check had an unbalanced one, `\left\{a\right.` in a fraction; and 9 of the neighbors' rule and of the scripts' parentheses as written with it (`neighbors.log`), each caught.

## Pandoc facts

This file's Pandoc facts are all in PANDOC-NOTES now (a8acfe7, 2026-10-14), each measured again there with 3.12.1 and saying which parts were, so read them there. Three of mine didn't hold, and measured again here with 3.12.1 (2026-10-14), they don't:

- **A prefixed `<m:math>` is read as MathML.** I had it read as no formula at all. The reader drops every tag's prefix first (`stripPrefixes`), and `<m:math>` holding `<m:mi>` reads as a formula, inline and display, its namespace declared on it, on `<html>`, or nowhere. What I measured before isn't known. The unpacker writes MathML unprefixed all the same.
- **lxml.html reads a self-closing `<mspace/>` as closed.** I had it nesting the rest of the paragraph inside. With lxml 5.2.1 (libxml2 2.12.6) and 6.1.3 (2.14.6), `lxml.html.fromstring`, `document_fromstring`, and `lxml.etree.HTML` close it, and `none`, `mprescripts`, `malignmark`, and the other elements tried. What I saw before isn't known either. `util/cnx-compare-word.py` still reads a page as XML, since that's how it finds a formula, by its namespace; its comment no longer gives the wrong reason.
- **A `<pre>`'s and its `<code>`'s classes aren't merged**: `pre`'s win where both have one, so `<pre class="x"><code class="language-python">` is a code block of class `x` alone. OpenStax names a program's language as a class of its code element (`python`, `r`), which the unpacker puts on the `<pre>` too, so no block of the books loses it.

One more, for PANDOC-NOTES, whose entry on `<pre>` says 3.9 is said to read one without a `<code>` as a `CodeBlock`, not measured. Measured with 3.9, TI's minimum (its release binary, 2026-10-14): a `<pre>` without a `<code>` is a `CodeBlock` (`plain` and an indented `two` as one block of two lines, where 3.12.1 makes a paragraph of no-break spaces and a `LineBreak`), and a `<pre>` with any attribute of its own takes none of its `<code>`'s: `<pre id="p2"><code class="python">` is a code block with the id and no class, so no language, where 3.12.1 gives it both, and `<pre class="x" id="p1"><code class="y" data-n="3">` loses `data-n` too. Read so in 3.9's `pCodeBlock` (the code's attributes are read only when the `pre` has none). The unpacker's blocks keep their language either way, their class being on the `<pre>`.

And one more, for PANDOC-NOTES: **the HTML writer writes a table's `summary` as `data-summary`.** `toAttrs` (`Writers/HTML.hs`, 3.12.1) prefixes `data-` to an attribute HTML5 doesn't have, and `summary` is in `html4Attributes` alone (`XML.hs`); it looks for a repeat by the name it read, so a table with both `summary` and `data-summary` gets `data-summary` twice, which isn't valid HTML. Read and measured, 2026-10-15. So an HTML source's summary reaches the page where a screen reader doesn't read it, as enki writes OpenStax's on purpose (open questions, the step tables).

## TextbookImprover observations

From converting the CNX books with `main`'s `convert.py`, validators on. PROJECT-NOTES has them in brief since 2026-10-14 (OpenStax's books from their source, through the checks); the detail is here.

- **`[html-raw] … iframe x1`** is the closing `</iframe>` fragment being counted, the frame itself made an embed. Tested as such (`"iframe x1" in marked.stderr`); misleading to read, but deliberate.
- **vnu's "Text run starts with a composing character"** on every formula with a hat written as U+0302 in an `<mo>` (Business Statistics: 33 warnings). Ties to the slides session's Round 7 decision (B, U+0302 kept for ŷ).
- **Alt text over 120 characters** is the commonest finding on OpenStax books (Business Statistics: 194 images), since OpenStax's alt texts are long descriptions. `image-alt-missing.csv` lists them as "too long".
- **The micro sign** (µ, U+00B5) for mu is repaired to Greek μ by `math.repair_equations`, in 75 of Business Statistics' formulas.
- **vnu's "Section lacks heading"** on every page with footnotes (Economics 3e: three pages), Pandoc's footnotes section. Already in SLIDES-PLAN's "not fixed" list. Gone since 1edb278 (2026-10-15), which heads a page's notes `Notes` (`notes.title`): converted again with it, *Entrepreneurship*'s 72 such warnings, one a page with notes, are none.
- **Economics 3e and Sociology 3e with validators on**: Sociology nothing found (243 pages); Economics the three warnings above and one table with neither headers nor caption (`chapter-12#table-5`, a payoff matrix in an answer), which now gets its summary as its caption.
- **Introduction to Python Programming, Nutrition for Nurses, and Principles of Data Science with validators on** (131, 195, and 105 pages, their bank exercises missing here). Python: nothing from vnu or the output check but one table with neither headers nor caption. Data Science: vnu's composing-character warning (above) on 257 formulas, and three footnote sections. Nutrition: four vnu errors, and four epubcheck errors in its EPUB, each a link from an address the source writes as text with a typo (`https://doi.org:10.1016/…`, a colon for a slash, read as a port), linked as cookbook's `post_bake` links it. - **A table marked as layout, from any HTML source** (`main` at a494d8b, 2026-10-15). A page of four two-column step tables, one `role="presentation"`, one `role="none"` (ARIA's other name for it), one with an `aria-label`, and one unmarked, converted to HTML: the census skips the first two and has one row for the other two, which are alike. The output check skips the first alone, so the `role="none"` table is a `table-without-headers-or-caption`, as are the other two, an `aria-label` not counting as a name. `figures-and-tables.lua` treats all four as data tables: each is in `table-captions-missing.csv`, warned of as having no header row and no declaration, and wrapped in a focusable scroll region; so would be the derivations DCIC's site profile marks layout (not run here, DCIC not being here). The filter counts a layout table in its page's position keys (here `steps#table-1`), so a change that stopped counting it would move the key of every table after it on the page, and the sidecar rows keyed on them. And no sidecar can say a table is layout: `table-headers.csv` takes `first-row`, `first-column`, `both`, and `none` (and keeps `manual` and `list`), so a Word source's layout table, of which Word records nothing (troubleshooting), can't be one. Item 20 under Fixes for `main` settles each of these.
- **A table with no column widths runs off a PDF's page** (`main` at 7a4e90e, 2026-10-16). Pandoc writes a table whose columns have no widths, and each of whose cells is one paragraph with no line break or is empty, as a longtable of `l`, `c`, or `r` columns (`isSimpleTable` and `colDescriptors`, Writers/LaTeX/Table.hs, 3.12), which don't wrap; any other table without widths gets `p` columns of equal width, which do. *Prealgebra 2e*'s Table 3.2, a worked example's steps, prints "The temperature warmed up 12 degrees from 7 degrees below zero." past the right edge of the page, before the layout-table change and after it. So would any such table with a long cell, from a source that gives no widths. Fixed for `main`, item 24.
- **A PDF numbers a data table that has an id and no caption** (`main` at d21f490, 2026-10-15). Pandoc's LaTeX writer holds such a table's id in an empty caption, `\caption{}\label{…}` (Writers/LaTeX/Table.hs, 3.12), which LaTeX numbers: a page of two data tables, the first with an id and no caption and the second with the caption "Costs by year", gives "Table 1" alone above the first and "Table 2: Costs by year" above the second. A table classed `unnumbered` gets no empty caption, and no `\label`, so its id goes nowhere in the PDF. In the dev-math books, one data table each in *Prealgebra 2e* and *Elementary Algebra 2e* has an id, no caption, and no class `unnumbered`, each in an answer on the answer key's page for a chapter; none of their tables classed `unnumbered` is a link's target (the 109 links to a table in the three books go to captioned data tables). Item 20 makes a layout table's id an anchor before it, and item 23 a data table's without a caption, which LaTeX numbers no longer.

Not fixed: where such a row goes, a body of its own or the table's foot, is the roadmap's open question for a trailing summary row's empty header cell, which it says to settle once for both (PROJECT-NOTES). Since item 51, the guess gives a table with such notes before its last row no header column, so Table 3.1's notes keep their span.
